topic: Albania's sworn virgins - women who legally became men under the Kanun
title: The Albanian Law That Let Women Legally Become Men
description: AI-narrated commentary exploring the Albanian Kanun tradition, where women could take a lifelong vow of celibacy to be recognized and live legally and socially as men. Original commentary inspired by a historical topic, not a reused clip or transcript.

hook_candidates.text: In parts of Albania, women could legally become men - just by swearing to never marry.
What if the only way to inherit your father's house was to legally stop being a woman?
You'd think gender was fixed by birth everywhere in history - one Albanian law said otherwise.
A woman stands before the village elders, swears she'll never marry, and from that day on lives entirely as a man.

beats.text: In the mountains of northern Albania, a woman could legally become a man — just by swearing never to marry.
It's called a 'sworn virgin,' under an old tribal code called the Kanun.
Under that law, women couldn't own land or inherit without a male relative in the house.
So a family with no sons could have a daughter swear lifelong celibacy instead.

beats.text: From then on she lived and was treated as a man — rifle, farmland, a seat with the men.
beats.broll_query: woman in traditional male shepherd clothing mountains

beats.text: It wasn't about identity — it was a legal loophole to save the family line.
A few sworn virgins still live in Albania today, the last of a fading tradition.
